findings.title: Emails use raw `guests` instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` receives the original input list, not `uniqueGuests`. If the input includes someone who is already an attendee, that person is treated as a brand-new guest and gets a fresh `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of the 'guests added' update. The intended split between new and existing attendees is therefore wrong whenever the input overlaps the current attendee list.

findings.title: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive
findings.body: The blacklist entries are lowercased, but each `guest` is compared as-is. A blacklisted address written with any uppercase letter (e.g. `Bad@x.com`) passes the filter. The attendee check `guest === attendee.email` is also case-sensitive, so an existing attendee can be added again as a duplicate by changing the casing. Normalize guest emails to lowercase before both comparisons.

findings.title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials, not the organizer's
findings.body: The `EventManager` is built from `ctx.user` and that user's credentials. When a team admin or an attendee (both allowed by the permission check) adds guests, the booking's calendar and video references belong to the organizer. `updateCalendarAttendees` will either fail or touch the wrong account. The organizer's credentials (`booking.user.credentials`) should be used instead.

findings.title: Calendar update failure after DB write leaves inconsistent state
findings.body: Attendees are inserted with `prisma.booking.update` before `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` runs, and that call is not wrapped in error handling. If the calendar update throws, the client sees an error, yet the guests are already saved and no emails are sent. A retry then fails with `emails_must_be_unique_valid` because the guests now exist. Wrap the call in error handling or order the operations so the result stays consistent.

findings.title: Team admin/owner check uses AND instead of OR
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`, so it is only true when both checks pass. The name and intent call for OR. Depending on how `isTeamAdmin` is implemented, plain team admins are denied permission they are meant to have.

findings.title: Any attendee can add unlimited arbitrary emails, enabling spam
findings.body: Any attendee of a booking may call this endpoint. The schema puts no limit on the number of guests, and the handler does not check booking status (cancelled, past, etc.). Each call sends emails from the platform to arbitrary addresses, so the endpoint can be abused to send spam. Add a maximum list size and a status check, and reconsider whether attendees should have this permission.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores event-type email-disable settings
findings.body: Every other booking email sender checks `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` and `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` against the event type metadata. `sendAddGuestsEmails` accepts no metadata and always emails organizers, team members and attendees. This sends mail even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

findings.title: Error fallback message is unreachable
findings.body: `message` is a template string such as `"undefined: ..."`, which is always truthy. As a result, `t("unable_to_add_guests")` is never shown, and users can see text like 'undefined: ...'.

findings.title: Validation error is never cleared after a successful submit
findings.body: `isInvalidEmail` is set to true on a failed validation. It is only reset by the Cancel button, not when the input is corrected, when a submit succeeds, or when the dialog is closed via `onOpenChange`. A stale 'Emails must be unique and valid' warning therefore stays visible after the problem is fixed.
